claims.text: A lighthouse keeper climbs the tower stairs in a storm and lights the lamp.
The tower interior is a spiral stone stairwell with an iron handrail, and the lamp room contains a brass fuel valve and a large glass lens.

constraints.text: Do not add spoken or sung lines.

description.text: A gaunt lighthouse keeper in a heavy oilskin coat shoulders open the tower door at the foot of a spiral stone stairwell, and cold rain blows in with him. One gloved hand finds the iron handrail as he starts to climb, the lantern on his belt swinging against his hip. Lightning flares white through the rain-lashed windows and the dark stone closes back around him.
The keeper pushes the door open and steps onto the wet first stair.
Rain hammers the narrow windows and the heavy door thuds shut below.

Lower on the curving steps, the keeper climbs steadily upward through a draught that snaps his coat tails and mists his breath. He leans into the turn, shoulder close to the cold wall, grip tightening on the iron rail as the tower shudders. Wind howls down the stairwell and the glass beside him rattles, but he keeps his eyes on the next landing.
The keeper leans into the curve and climbs, boots finding each worn tread.
Wind buffets the stairwell and loose glass rattles in its frame.

In the lamp room, the keeper sets the lantern on a work ledge and bends over the brass fuel valve, opening it with quick, practiced turns. Rain streams down the glass panes around him while the great lens waits dark beside his shoulder. He trims the wick with small steel scissors, shaping the flame to come, and checks the burner with a careful thumb.
The keeper opens the brass valve and listens to the fuel line tick.
Metal creaks open, the wick scissors snip, and rain drums on the lantern glass.

The keeper strikes a match and touches it to the wick; flame catches with a soft whump and swells across the burner. He steps back as the lens begins to turn, throwing a broad beam through the streaming glass and out over the black, storm-torn sea. Far below, waves break white against the rocks, and the new light sweeps across them in a long, deliberate arc.
The match flares and the keeper guides it to the waiting wick.
Wind and surf roar far below while the tower glass hums in the gale.

soundscape: Storm-driven rain and wind surround the tower, with muffled thunder, water dripping on stone, boots on wet steps, creaking iron, snipping scissors, a match strike, a soft flame whump, and the low mechanical turn of the lens.
music: A restrained orchestral score: a low string drone, slow timpani pulses, and a rising brass swell when the lamp ignites.
